errors.english: Only stay until it is born,
errors.why: The Tibetan describes the just-born fawn that she will lick with her tongue and suckle; it is not a request to wait until the birth.

errors.english: Seeing the doe anguished for her child speaking in this manner
errors.why: The narrator's closing passage on the Bodhisattva's compassion is verse (eleven-syllable lines through the side's end) but is rendered as prose.

note: A faithful rendering of the doe's plea; one misconstrued verse line and the final verse passage given as prose.

errors.english: In reply to the claim that contradiction consists precisely in the distinction between a cause that acts after enduring and its effect
errors.why: The Tibetan says the text's own reply ('Fire...') is that contradiction is a particular kind of cause-effect relation in which the cause acts after enduring; it is not an opponent's claim being answered.

fix.find: In reply to the claim that contradiction consists precisely in the distinction between a cause that acts after enduring and its effect
fix.replace: Replying that contradiction is precisely a particular kind of cause-and-effect relation, in which the cause acts after enduring [for some moments]

note: A careful rendering of a dense ṭīkā on the fire-and-cold example; one reply misread as the opponent's claim.

errors.english: entered exactly as the divine command had instructed
errors.why: In this drama ལྷ (deva) is the form of address for the king; Subāhu acts on His Majesty's order, not a divine command.

errors.english: Come Indra, come Hari [note: Vishnu], see the sheep and the bulls!
errors.why: This is the Vedic subrahmaṇyā invocation of Indra (hari-vaḥ 'lord of bay horses', 'ram of Medhātithi'), so 'Hari' is not Vishnu and 'see the sheep and the bulls' is a guess.

note: The drama's action, verses and speakers are rendered correctly; a court-address term and the Vedic mantra gloss are off.

errors.english: similarity in being an effect
errors.why: The word completes མི་རྟག་ from the previous side: the similarity is in impermanence (mi rtag pa nyid) and so on, not in being an effect.

note: A sound rendering of the aviśeṣasama discussion; only the boundary word was guessed wrongly.

errors.english: Just as there is no physical obstruction in space, so too is their mind.
errors.why: The stock simile is of a hand moving unobstructed through space (the mind like a hand in space); the hand is dropped.

note: Accurate gloss-by-gloss rendering of the arhat epithets, with standard Vinaya and Abhidharma terms handled correctly.

errors.english: It is said that one desires to [note: attain the result].
errors.why: The words complete the opponent's thesis from the previous side, that the inner sense bases are held to arise ultimately as well, not a desire to attain a result.

fix.find: It is said that one desires to [note: attain the result].
fix.replace: So they say: [the inner sense bases] are held to arise [ultimately as well].

errors.english: if the result like a sprout does not arise from discordant conditions, then this becomes an opening for logical challenge
errors.why: The Tibetan asks why the sprout would not arise from discordant conditions too, and that question is what opens the statement to challenge; the English makes it a conditional with the opposite sense.

fix.find: if the result like a sprout does not arise from discordant conditions, then this becomes an opening for logical challenge
fix.replace: why would the result, such as a sprout, not arise from discordant conditions too? So the statement becomes one open to challenge

note: The verse and the Bhāviveka-Avalokitavrata argument are mostly clear, but the opening is misglossed and one key sentence is inverted.

errors.english: This is because they are not the actual thing as it is.
errors.why: 'Because it would not accord with the object' is said of a sense cognition that takes a universal as its object, not of the universal and particular.

errors.english: One should say that it takes the particular specifically.
errors.why: The text says that this very point ('according with the object') should be stated as a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa) in the definition of perception, as the gloss that follows shows.

errors.english: Direct perception is the result of direct perception.
errors.why: The lemma means that the result of perception is figuratively called 'perception' (as the next side discusses), not that perception is its own result.

note: The anti-realist argument about universals is followed, but several glosses on the lemmas are misconstrued.

errors.english: If there were a distinction, it would be the (Vedavadin) one who upholds the Vedas who is established by intrinsic nature.
errors.why: རིག་བྱེད་པ here means Vedic statements (vaidika), not a person: the opponent's distinction is that the Vedic statement is self-established (unauthored).

fix.find: If there were a distinction, it would be the (Vedavadin) one who upholds the Vedas who is established by intrinsic nature.
fix.replace: If [it is said that] there is a distinction, namely that the Vedic [statement] is established by its own nature:

errors.english: between the meanings of the worldly ones and the (Veda) followers
errors.why: The contrast is between worldly (laukika) and Vedic (vaidika) statements, not between worldly people and Veda followers.

fix.find: between the meanings of the worldly ones and the (Veda) followers
fix.replace: between the meanings of worldly and Vedic statements

errors.english: no distinction is seen between the followers of the (Veda) and the worldly ones
errors.why: The statement is that no distinction is seen between Vedic and worldly statements.

fix.find: no distinction is seen between the followers of the (Veda) and the worldly ones
fix.replace: no distinction is seen between Vedic and worldly statements

errors.english: If one asks whether whatever is not like that must be man-made
errors.why: This is the opponent's assertion ('whatever is not so is man-made'), not a question.

errors.english: if the established vow exists
errors.why: དམ་བཅས་པ here is the convention (samaya) set by powerful persons that makes mantras effective, not a vow.

note: The anti-apauruṣeya argument is followed, but vaidika is systematically rendered as 'Veda followers' and the convention term is mistranslated.

errors.english: Those who give rise to such things are called thus.
errors.why: The verb completes དགེ་བ་དྲུངས་ from the previous side: those who uproot virtue (dge ba drungs 'byin pa), not those who give rise to things.

fix.find: Those who give rise to such things are called thus.
fix.replace: Those who uproot virtue are called thus.

errors.english: because one slanders all phenomena, they possess no self-nature, and are thus like a flower seen in the sky
errors.why: It is the nihilist himself who, by denying all phenomena, is of the nature of nonexistence and so like a sky-flower; the phenomena are not the subject.

fix.find: because one slanders all phenomena, they possess no self-nature, and are thus like a flower seen in the sky
fix.replace: because one who denies all phenomena is himself of the nature of nonexistence, he is like a flower in the sky

errors.english: (nikaya-sabhaga-bija)
errors.why: རིགས་མཐུན་པའི་ས་བོན is a homogeneous seed (sabhāga-bīja); nikāyasabhāga is a different Abhidharma term (group homogeneity).

errors.english: The Hailstone of the Sublime Dharma
errors.why: The epithet is 'hail on the crop of the true Dharma'; with 'crop' dropped, the Dharma becomes the hail rather than what is destroyed.

errors.english: the conceptualization of material things and so forth
errors.why: དངོས་པོ here is 'entity/existent' (bhāva) in the conceptions of entity and so on; 'material' is added and skews the argument for rebirth.

note: The rebirth syllogism is followed, but the opening epithets are misread and a key seed term is misglossed.

errors.english: it is a single part of the ultimate truth
errors.why: This is the fault 'part of the thesis' (pratijñārthaikadeśa; དམ་པའི་ is a slip for དམ་བཅའི་, as དམ་བཅས་པའི་དོན་གྱི་ཕྱོགས་གཅིག in the next sentence confirms), not ultimate truth.

fix.find: it is a single part of the ultimate truth
fix.replace: it is a part of the thesis

errors.english: Because there is no difference between the object to be remembered and the object to be proven, it cannot be expressed.
errors.why: དེ་ལྟར་དྲན་བྱ means the earlier fault 'is to be recalled here likewise'; the reason, being non-different from the probandum, cannot be stated. There is no 'object to be remembered'.

errors.english: we reply:
errors.why: The verse ('for you there is no universal of cognition') is the rejoinder that the author then rejects with 'This is not reasonable... it is not that we do not accept', so it is not the author's reply.

note: The PVA dialectic is mostly tracked, but a standard thesis-fault term is mistranslated and the dialogue roles blur.
